extracted.intended_audience: educators, philosophers, and students of education (readers of philosophy of education)
extracted.subtask_description: Extracts criteria about what counts as genuine knowledge and how philosophy should inform educational aims and methods; focuses on continuity vs dualism, methods of knowing, and the educative implications of different epistemologies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Philosophy as the general theory of education
rubrics_metrics.description: If a theory makes no difference in educational endeavor, it must be artificial. Philosophy may even be defined as the general theory of education.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Philosophy must not remain symbolic or merely verbal; its auditing of experience and program of values must take effect in conduct. Educational equivalents are necessary to translate philosophical critique and interpretation of science into practice; public agitation and administrative action are effective only insofar as they are educative. Example: youth education offers a fairer field for forming dispositions than attempts to change habits of adults.

rubrics_metrics.name: Philosophic thinking should address social uncertainties and be tested in action
rubrics_metrics.description: Philosophic thinking is a form of thinking which finds its origin in what is uncertain in experience, aims to locate the nature of the perplexity and to frame hypotheses for its clearing up to be tested in action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Theorizing must be connected to widespread social difficulties and organizational conflicts; hypotheses should lead to educative practice and be evaluated by their effects in conduct rather than remaining mere speculation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Philosophy must criticize existing aims relative to scientific resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Philosophy has a double task: criticizing existing aims with respect to the existing state of science, pointing out obsolete values, and interpreting results of specialized science in their bearing on future social endeavor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This requires educational methods to instantiate the revised aims; philosophy cannot 'summon' values into existence without educative work to form dispositions compatible with those values.

rubrics_metrics.name: Favor continuity over dualism in theories of knowing
rubrics_metrics.description: The preferred theory assumes continuity; many traditional theories state or imply certain basic divisions, separations, or antitheses (dualisms), which are problematic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that social divisions (class, gender, status) produce dualistic philosophies. Avoid theories that posit hard separations (e.g., appearance vs inaccessible essence) or require flight to a transcendental realm to escape dualism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid the empirical vs higher rational knowing split
rubrics_metrics.description: Opposition between empirical (everyday, utilitarian knowing) and higher rational knowing (theoretical, pursued for its own sake) is a dualism that leads to depreciating practical intelligence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Educational practice should integrate both: particulars (empirical detail) and universals (general principles). Example: geography (particulars) and higher mathematics (universals) are complementary rather than separate worlds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reject knowledge-as-storage vs knowing-as-active dichotomy
rubrics_metrics.description: One sense of learning is the sum total of what is known (external storage); the other is active, personally conducted knowing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid pedagogy that treats learning as drawing on a ready-made store. Emphasize active, constructive study where the individual's activity produces understanding. Anti-pattern: treating appropriation of book material as the endpoint of education.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasize active (not passive) modes of knowing
rubrics_metrics.description: Dualism of activity and passivity: physical things are thought known by impressions; rational knowledge is thought to spring from internal activity remote from senses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor sense training, object lessons, and laboratory exercises over exclusively book-based, passive instruction. Teaching should acknowledge that nervous-system-mediated activity and motor responses shape knowing (example: carpenter or etcher whose motor responses shape subsequent sensory stimuli).

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrate intellect and emotions in education
rubrics_metrics.description: Opposition between intellect (pure apprehension of truth) and emotions (private, personal concerns) leads to depreciation of interest yet reliance on extrinsic rewards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not decry appeal to interest while endorsing examinations, marks, prizes, and punishments. Cultivate intrinsic interest and avoid crippling teachers' sense of humor or overreliance on extraneous incentives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unify knowing and doing (theory and practice)
rubrics_metrics.description: The separation of knowing and doing—mind as end and body as means—produces educational evils; knowing should reorganize activity rather than be isolated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design curricula that connect intellectual understanding with practical action; value responsibility emerging from continuity of action where earlier acts prepare later ones (basis of all responsibility).

rubrics_metrics.name: Knowledge must reorganize activity (neuroscience and continuity)
rubrics_metrics.description: Knowledge is connected to nervous system functions that effect reciprocal adjustment between stimuli and responses; the brain reorganizes activity to maintain continuity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pedagogy should reflect that mental activity is integrated with motor responses and that each action shapes subsequent perception; learning-by-doing and sequential, cumulative tasks exemplify this continuity (carpenter example).

rubrics_metrics.name: Evolutionary continuity implies knowledge as participation in the world
rubrics_metrics.description: Evolution emphasizes continuity from simpler to more complex forms; as activity becomes complex, intelligence forecasts and shapes future consequences, making knowledge a mode of participation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Education should prepare learners to identify with their environment, forecast outcomes, and shape actions accordingly—moving beyond spectator notions of knowing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experimental method as central criterion of knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: The experimental method means (i) calling knowledge only where activity has produced physical changes that confirm conception and (ii) thinking is of avail when anticipations based on observation guide trials; experiment is trial of ideas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Teach and apply experimental inquiry across physical, social, and moral domains; reward thoughtful trials where consequences are noted and used to inform future predictions. Anti-pattern: relying on dogma or authority instead of trials of thought.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reject scholastic/formal-discipline methods unconnected to experience
rubrics_metrics.description: Scholastic method (formal discipline) systematizes material accepted on authority and often makes distinctions, definitions, and classifications for their own sake with no objective in experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid teaching that emphasizes formal logical operations detached from substantive subject matter. The doctrine of formal discipline treats thought as a seal stamped on any material—this is criticized if disconnected from practical aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance particularizing (sensory discrimination) and generalizing (reason)
rubrics_metrics.description: Real knowledge requires particulars (discriminated by senses) and generalities (connections brought by reason); both functions must work together.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Instruction should develop capacity to specify facts clearly AND to use past organized experience (general principles) to give meaning to new particulars. Anti-patterns: sensationalism (only particulars) and rationalism (only general relations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Knowledge judged by increased control and experienced significance
rubrics_metrics.description: Two aspects of knowledge's value: (i) increased power of control (practical efficacy) and (ii) increased meaning attaching to experience (mental reward even when practical failure occurs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design learning experiences that enhance learners' capacity to manage situations and to derive meaning; do not conflate mere possession of facts with practical understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prospective reference: knowledge must be applicable to future action
rubrics_metrics.description: While content of knowledge is what has happened, its reference is future or prospective—knowledge furnishes means of understanding what is still going on and what is to be done.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate and teach knowledge by its usefulness in interpreting and acting upon unfolding situations rather than as static possession about the past.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pragmatic test of knowledge (utility in reorganizing experience)
rubrics_metrics.description: The pragmatic view: knowledge consists of intellectual resources—habits and dispositions that render action intelligent by enabling adaptation of environment and aims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt pragmatic standards in assessing knowledge: prefer ideas that reorganize experience and make past experiences available for novel situations. Instruction should cultivate dispositions enabling flexible adaptation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Counteract one-sided intelligence produced by social divisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Social divisions that interfere with free intercourse make intelligence one-sided (practical empiricists vs contemplative rationalists; realists vs idealists).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Educational programs should provide experiences that broaden outlooks across class-conditioned perspectives and integrate practical, contemplative, and interpretive modes of intelligence.
